diagnosis: Type I Hiatal Hernia with GERD

patient.key: Overweight patient, chest pain with GERD symptoms (heartburn, regurgitation, dysphagia). Dysphagia is an alarm symptom. Office setting. Type I hiatal hernia (sliding) — gastric cardia herniates through the esophageal hiatus. Accounts for 95% of hiatal hernias. Type I = medical management (PPI/H2 blocker). Types II-IV = surgical.

ordersPlaced: Physical exam: General, Chest/Lungs, Heart, Abdomen
correctlyOrdered: Physical Exam: General, Chest/Lungs, Heart, Abdomen

missedOrders.why: Dysphagia is an ALARM symptom. Cannot empirically treat GERD when the patient has dysphagia — needs structural evaluation to rule out stricture, malignancy, or motility disorder. Also: must confirm Type I (medical) vs Type II-IV (surgical). Type I = PPI only. Types II-IV = surgical repair. The management fork is binary, and you cannot choose without visualizing the hernia.
Chest pain = rule out cardiac causes. GERD and CAD can coexist, and the history of 'heartburn' can be misleading. An EKG is fast, noninvasive, and necessary for any chest pain presentation.
Screen for anemia from chronic GI blood loss. GERD can cause erosive esophagitis with occult bleeding.
Basic chemistry panel. Renal function is relevant for any patient on long-term medications.
Weight loss directly reduces GERD symptoms. Overweight patient — this is preventive care and treatment combined.

teachingPoints: Treatment 100%, diagnosis 13%. You treated something you never confirmed. Dysphagia means you must visualize the esophagus.
Type I hiatal hernia (95% of cases) = sliding, gastric cardia herniates, managed with PPI/H2 blocker. Types II-IV = surgical. You cannot tell which type without imaging.
Dysphagia is an ALARM SYMPTOM in GERD. It demands endoscopic or radiographic evaluation — not empirical PPI trial.
Chest pain always gets an EKG. Even when the history sounds GI. Even in the office setting.
The mirror of the AFib case: in AFib you diagnosed perfectly and forgot treatment. Here you treated perfectly and forgot diagnosis. Both fail.

typeI.description: Sliding — gastric cardia herniates through esophageal hiatus
typeI.management: Medical: PPI, H2 blocker, lifestyle. No surgery.

typeII.description: Paraesophageal — gastric fundus herniates through phrenoesophageal membrane defect

typeIII.description: Mixed — both Type I (sliding cardia) and Type II (fundus herniation)

typeIV.description: Other organs herniate (colon, spleen, small intestine, pancreas)
